While Sebastian led the boy away,
he gave the boy some coins and came
back with a basket of kittens. The girls
were excited to see the animals, but Miss
Rottenmeier's anger was aroused again.
She said that Heidi must be punished.
But Clara insisted they wait for her father to make the decision. When Mr.
Sesemann returned, he asked for both Miss Rottenmeier and Clara's opinions
of Heidi, which were totally different. But through all the stories Clara told him
about Heidi and his own observations, Mr. Sesemann decided that Heidi was a
different yet innocent girl.
"I would like Heidi to stay," he announced in the evening. "Clara loves
having her around. Please be nice to her," he said to Miss Rottenmeier. "By the
way, my mother will visit soon, so she will take the burden off you a bit," he
continued.
Heidi liked Grandmamma right away. The old lady was kind and she cared
about Heidi. When she realized that Heidi didn't have much to do when Clara
took her afternoon rest, she read books to her. When Heidi begged her to read
more, Grandmamma had an idea.
"Why don't you try reading it yourself? You are smart. I'm sure you'll learn
it in no time," she encouraged Heidi.
That evening, Grandmamma gave Heidi the book with pictures of green
grass and goats as a present.
